result.summary:
End-to-end verification of partura-steering (HEAD 9aa7e2a) on a synthetic cube + synthetic DailyFieldStore, driven by six scripts under /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/verify_e2e/ (run_all.sh; 193 checks, all green). Nothing tracked was modified: /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering is clean and `pytest tests/ -q` is 923 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed at 9aa7e2a (no new failures; the 617-test baseline is a subset). /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube was only read, and used as a comparison arm.

(1) Expressions (p1, 58 checks). div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap), cs_regres(day_max(Ret), FloatCap) (the registry has no cs_bucket_rank — it is a Partura kernel — so the binary cs_* slot used cs_regres, as the task allows), ts_delta(FloatCap, 5), cross_mean(LimitWidth, 5), day_mean(mul(Ret, LimitWidth)), bare FloatCap and ts_delta(LogFloatCap, 1) all parse strict, plan as P[2] -> S[5] -> P[2], and evaluate. Numerics match hand-written numpy (max abs 0 for ts_delta/cross_mean/bare/log, 6.4e-8 for the turnover factor, 9.5e-12 for day_mean(mul(...))); the cs_regres residual is orthogonal to the daily leaf on all 40 days. Chunk invariance is exactly 0.0 under chunk_symbols=3/1, chunk_days=7/1 and 2/5. A non-ascending symbol subset keeps the caller's order and its daily plane equals the full plane's rows; a warmed_view window's plane equals the full plane's window and every non-cross-sectional root matches exactly after the trim. day_sum(FloatCap) / in_mean_rolling(FloatCap, 5) / nt_ts_mean(FloatCap, 5) are refused in both modes with a message naming the leaf and the reason ("... needs genuine per-minute variation, but FloatCap is a daily-only field with no minute axis at all"); in_mean is not a registered name, so in_mean_rolling stood in. tolerant=True turns a stored field with no daily store into an error row instead of a crash, and LimitWidth still resolves with no daily store attached.

(2) Plugin (p2 library 47 checks, p3 CLI 31 checks). A plugin module registering one real_valued kernel at import time, a scorer kind that cuts its own train/valid split from dates/warmup, a SearchHooks(op_weight, accept, daily_fields, daily_leaf_prob, leaf_slots) and a seed list. Verified: load_plugins after default_registry() was already built still works and resets the cache; the declared kernel is in searchable(include_boolean=False, include_resource_risk=False) while its byte-identical undeclared twin is not (the declaration is load-bearing: 214 -> 221); declare_real_valued's by-name channel reaches in_sustain_{mean,stddev,product}; scorer_kinds() carries the new kind and the factory gets dates=view.dates with the warmup given, dates[warmup] being the first evaluated day; the generator receives op_weight/accept/daily_fields/leaf_slots and hook_rng is a separate stream; the boosted plugin operator is drawn by _pick and reaches real trees (1603/4000 draws at 60x); weight-0 operators appear in 0 of 4000 draws and in none of 370 trees across all generations; no evaluated or archived tree carries a structure accept refuses, and every non-None child of mutate_window/subtree/operator/hoist/crossover satisfies accept (the two previously-leaking mutations were exercised directly on hook-refused carriers: 0 children with the hook, 180 without); the registered scorer's columns land in archive_gen*.csv as score_e2e_train/score_e2e_valid with values in every row; wall_seconds=0.001 stops at 1 of a planned 100 generations with report.stopped_early == "wall clock" while wall_seconds=0 runs the whole budget; GenerationExhausted fires under on_exhausted="raise" and the default fallback counts unaccepted_fallbacks == 1. Through the CLI, --plugin and $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS both load the module, both deliver search_hooks(), and their archives are byte-identical at the same seed.

(3) Reproducibility and the control arm (p3). The same CLI command twice gives byte-identical archive_gen*.csv, members.csv, combination.csv and the same meta.json pool metrics / rejections / contract hash. With no plugin and no --daily-fields, the branch's run is byte-identical to the same command on the baseline worktree (517fd09) at the same seed, across all three artefacts.

Also verified (p4/p6): --ban now validates on the RL branch too; BatchRewarder(accept=...) refuses with its own reason before the engine call; research and calculate both evaluate/export a daily-leaf factor through --daily-fields; $ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS alone attaches the store; contract_hash moves only with a daily source; view_cache_key(daily=None) is byte-identical and a fingerprint changes it; a DF: ban key passes check_ban_key, is rejected when the field is a typo, and really bans the structure through a full --ban + --ban-rank-corr + --ban-archive block-to-block inheritance run (the standing rolling-block rule).

Two deviations from the design text, source taken as authoritative. (a) hook_rng: the design's literal random.Random((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF) is replaced by generator._hook_seed, derived from the rng stream's state; its docstring records that gp.py passes rng= and never seed=, so the literal formula gave every run the identical hook stream and at seed 0 that stream was self._rng itself. Verified the shipped version is reproducible from the miner seed, varies with it, differs from the generator's own stream, and draining it does not move the tree stream. (b) The design's test plan says ShapeError for the rejected bare-leaf cases; make_node does raise ShapeError, but parse/parse_legacy wrap it in ParseError (ValueError) as the parser always has. Messages are specific either way.

One observation, pre-existing and not a defect of this branch: cs_regres(day_max(Ret), FloatCap) differs by 9.3e-10 absolute between a full view and a warm-up-extended window over the same days. The panel operands reach an nd kernel as transposed, non-contiguous float32 views, so the reduction over the symbol axis blocks differently for a (40, S) and a (33, S) tensor. Reproduced standalone with cs_regres on strided float32 at 1e9 magnitude, and with the minute-only operand mul(day_sum(Amt), 1e6) (4.66e-10), so the daily leaf did not introduce it. Chunk invariance within one view stays exactly 0.0.

ok=false only because of the four defects below; every behaviour items (1)-(3) asked for passes.

defects.title: op_weight never reaches the RL search: operator_logit_bias has no caller and no miner can take it
defects.failure_scenario: The design's "6. RL parity" states that "the miners derive logit_bias[i] = log(max(w, tiny)) once per OperatorToken from the same op_weight, added to the policy logits before action_mask is applied, so weight 0 becomes an effective mask", and WP10 step 5 adds the helper so "one shared op_weight then steers both searches". The helper exists (src/alphacube/mining/tokens.py:150) and is correct when called by hand — it returns log(1e-9) at a weight-0 operator's index — but `grep -rn --include=*.py operator_logit_bias src/` returns only its own definition: nothing in the tree consumes it. inspect.signature(AlphaGenMiner.__init__) has no bias/weight parameter at all, and pipeline.py:398 builds the Vocabulary and then `cls(vocab, rew, max_expr_len=..., seed=seed, **(rl_params or {}))` with no bias plumbing. Measured with a plugin whose op_weight zeroes day_mean/day_std/cs_rank/log: a real `cli mine --miner alphagen --plugin <mod>` run loads the plugin, runs its accept hook and its scorer, and leaves all four weight-0 operators as legal, unbiased OperatorTokens in the action space. A sweep that points one steer config at a GP arm and an RL arm therefore gets a steered GP arm and an unsteered RL arm, with nothing in stdout or meta.json distinguishing them. (WP10 is labelled OPTIONAL in the work-package list, but the design's RL-parity section states the behaviour unconditionally, so the two texts disagree.)
defects.suggested_fix: In pipeline.run_mining's RL branch compute `bias = operator_logit_bias(vocab, hooks.op_weight)` from the `hooks = cfg.get("hooks")` already read at pipeline.py:427, and give the TokenMiner base a `logit_bias=None` keyword that is added to the policy logits before action_mask is applied (one place, inherited by all five miners). If WP10 is to stay optional instead, make the silence loud: have cmd_mine / run_mining raise or say() when hooks.op_weight is not None and miner != "gp", and amend the design's RL-parity paragraph to match.

defects.title: hooks.daily_fields cannot reach an RL run: the only Vocabulary construction passes no daily_fields
defects.failure_scenario: WP10 steps 1-4 add `daily_fields` to Vocabulary.__init__, the DailyFeatureToken, the ExpressionBuilder branch and the dispatch, and the design's RL-parity section says "Vocabulary(..., daily_fields=()) adds DailyFeatureTokens". But pipeline.py:398 is the only Vocabulary(...) construction in the tree and it passes only n_minutes / allow_boolean_ops / allow_resource_risk; rl_params reach the miner class, not the vocabulary, so no CLI or library route can populate it. Verified: no DailyFeatureToken exists in the vocabulary the pipeline builds, and a real `cli mine --miner alphagen --daily-fields DIR --plugin <mod>` run attaches the daily store (the log names all nine fields), pays the changed contract_hash and exemplar-cache key for it, and then mines an action space in which no daily field appears — no daily leaf in its output, and no warning that the attached data is unreachable. The GP arm of the same config does get the daily leaves, so the two arms search different grammars for a reason nothing reports.
defects.suggested_fix: Pass `daily_fields=tuple(f for f in (hooks.daily_fields if hooks is not None else ()) if f in view.daily_fields)` into the Vocabulary at pipeline.py:398 (intersecting with view.daily_fields keeps unresolvable names out of the action space), and add a pipeline-level test alongside tests/test_daily_tokens.py's token-append test so the wiring is pinned rather than only the Vocabulary keyword.

defects.title: A steer config naming a stored daily field with no daily store attached burns budget silently
defects.failure_scenario: GPMiner forwards hooks.daily_fields / leaf_slots into TypedTreeGenerator without ever comparing them against what the view can resolve, and _panels evaluates with tolerant=True (gp.py:421). So with a --plugin whose search_hooks() names FloatCap/LogFloatCap and no --daily-fields (or a daily root missing those planes), dailyfields.resolve raises per candidate, the engine returns a None panel, the fitness is -inf and the tree vanishes. The run exits 0. Measured on a real CLI run: stdout's only daily line is "daily fields: none attached", meta.json says nothing, the archive is non-empty and contains no FloatCap expression, and nothing anywhere names the unresolvable field; through the library at daily_leaf_prob=0.35 it was 5 of 70 evaluated candidates (7%) spent on trees that cannot be evaluated at all, and the share scales with daily_leaf_prob. The design anticipates the adjacent failure (resolve warns once per field when a field's first finite date is after dates[0] — the silent-empty-warm-up case in `risks`) and adds the "daily fields <root>: ..." say() line so "a run log shows whether the data was actually found", but neither covers a hook asking for a field this run has no source for — which is the one a steer arm will hit, because the hook and the --daily-fields flag are set by different people at different times.
defects.suggested_fix: In GPMiner.__init__, right after the hooks are unpacked (gp.py:250), compute `missing = [f for f in hooks.daily_fields if f not in view.daily_fields]` plus the same over every field tuple in hooks.leaf_slots, and raise ValueError naming them and view.daily_fields — it is a configuration error in the same sense as an unknown op_weight key, which already raises. If raising is too strict for a sweep, say() it once at the top of the run and record the list in meta.json so an archived arm can be told apart from a steered one afterwards.

defects.title: leaf_slots and daily_fields get none of the construction-time validation op_weight gets
defects.failure_scenario: The design adds construction-time validation so that, in _resolve_op_weight's own words, "a typo'd name would otherwise sit silently inert, never matched against any real OpSpec": an op_weight mapping key must name a registered operator, values must be finite and >= 0, and accept must take exactly one positional parameter. All of those were verified to raise. But generator.py:216-218 stores `self.daily_fields = list(daily_fields)` and `self.leaf_slots = leaf_slots` raw. Verified: TypedTreeGenerator(reg, leaf_slots={"not_an_operator": {0: ("FloatCap",)}}) constructs without complaint and is silently inert, and so is a slot index outside the operator's arity; TypedTreeGenerator(reg, daily_fields=("NoSuchField",), daily_leaf_prob=1.0) constructs and builds trees like cross_regbeta(NoSuchField, NoSuchField, 241) that can only fail at evaluation. A reverse-guidance config that names a renamed operator or mis-spells a field therefore produces an arm that looks steered, reports no error, and is not steered — exactly the failure mode the op_weight key check was added to prevent. (The design states the validation list only for op_weight and accept, so this is an inconsistency in the guarantee rather than a broken promise.)
defects.suggested_fix: Extend the __init__ validation block (generator.py:216-230) to check leaf_slots keys against the registry (`name not in registry` -> ValueError naming it), each slot index against that spec's arity, and every field name in daily_fields and in leaf_slots' tuples against registry.daily_fields — the same error shape _resolve_op_weight already uses for an unknown operator name.
